main_body: Brick kitchen range: a brick chimney stack on top, a dark slate hood, a grey panel strip, and a brick base with a glowing firebox opening
top_band: none. Under the chimney, row 21 is a 1-row light edge (L126). Rows 22-25 are dark slate (L61), darker than the face and read as a sloped hood front. No lighter horizontal surface follows.
evidence: The column scan has no lighter multi-row top band. The only light row is the 1-row edge at row 21, and the hood rows under it (L61) are darker than the front, so they are a vertical or sloped front, not a surface seen from above. The chimney, panel strip and brick base with firebox are all flat vertical faces drawn face-on. The firebox is an inset frame but sits on a flat front. This matches the red front-elevation case in the guide.

style.evidence: 98% of the dark edge pixels are neutral, so the outline is near-black rather than the tinted dark material tone the references use. The candidate has only 14 distinct colours against 38-40 in the references. The brick and slate ramps are shallow, at about 3-4 steps each. The firebox flames are well shaded, and the median of 13 colours per tile is close to the references, but the sticker-like neutral outline and thinner ramps leave it below the Beodeul bar.
